metadata.title: HEIF Heist + OpenAI CISO disclosure: real RCE/SSO chain, burned Slack, Streisand, then an apology
metadata.frame: Hacktron AI (three researchers) chained a libheif heap overflow in Discourse (community.openai.com) with an OpenAI SSO flaw on 25 Jul 2026, proved access to OpenAI's internal monorepo via a harmless employee-Codex PR, stopped, and got a 14-hour OpenAI-side patch plus a $6,500 bounty (community.openai.com out of Bugcrowd scope). LiveOverflow's 19 Sep 2026 thread is the PROCESS layer: CISO Slack that felt antagonistic, 'stunt hacking document,' malicious compliance, WSJ exclusive, Vercel as the control case, Hugging Face incident as stress context, then a same-day apology. Technical chain = fact. 'CISO fumbled' = labeled personal opinion, later qualified. Overlay.
metadata.grade: RCE/SSO chain, PR-proof, 14h patch, $6,500 bounty, Discourse GHSA, HEIF Heist target list, token-cost claims = FACT (Hacktron blog; Discourse advisory; WSJ/Verge/TechCrunch). LiveOverflow Slack screenshots = his contemporaneous account, not an independent transcript. Causal 'WSJ happened because CISO was pissed' = HIS LABELED OPINION. Apology = his report of a private outreach the same day. Do not freeze the story at 'bridge burned.'
metadata.honest_limits: LiveOverflow is Hacktron-adjacent (named in the blog acknowledgements) - a party. Hacktron's July blog thanks OpenAI for speed; the September thread is the sour aftertaste; keep both. No exploit, no employee names, no repo contents. 'Algorithmic secrets' is WSJ anonymous sourcing. CISO not named in the thread; Dane Stuckey is OpenAI CISO in the separate HF postmortem coverage - this block does not turn Slack quotes into a person dossier. Overlay; excluded from proofs.
metadata.method: Hacktron 'Hacking OpenAI' (13 Sep 2026) + heif-heist.com; LiveOverflow thread 2101252692635004997 (19 Sep 2026) including the apology follow-up; Discourse GHSA-vhm9-85gw-x335; Vercel libheif blog; WSJ via Verge/TechCrunch/VentureBeat; Bugcrowd OpenAI engagement page.

edges.notes: Hacktron AI (Harsh Jaiswal, Mohan Pedhapati, Rahul Maini; assisted by Sudhanshu Rajbhar) named the campaign HEIF Heist: a class of remote attack paths against services that decode attacker-controlled HEIF/HEIC/AVIF via native libheif/libde265, usually pulled in through ImageMagick/libvips/Sharp/distro images (fact; heif-heist.com).

The vulnerable surface is below the app: libheif (and libde265) memory corruption on crafted overlay image items. Upstream had changed the code ~a year earlier without marking a security fix / CVE, so Debian 12/13 shipped vulnerable 1.19.7/1.19.8 in Discourse's Docker image. Not a single-version bug - families 1.19.x through 1.23.x; patch to current upstream (v1.23.2 then 1.23.4 by mid-Sep 2026) (fact; Hacktron; Debian DSA-6417-1).

Discourse HEIC uploads bypass FastImage and go to ImageMagick magick, which hands decoding to libheif - exposing the native parser to attacker-controlled files. GHSA-vhm9-85gw-x335 (28 Jul 2026); Discourse sandboxed ImageMagick as defense-in-depth. Self-hosters must rebuild the Docker image, not just click-update (fact).

community.openai.com is a Discourse-hosted forum with 'Sign in with OpenAI' (auth.openai.com). Compromising the forum was one path into OpenAI SSO, not the only conceivable one (Hacktron: any first/third-party service on that SSO would have yielded the same ChatGPT/Codex access) (fact of architecture; 'any service' is their claim).

25 Jul 2026, <72h: libheif RCE on community.openai.com -> OpenAI SSO flaw -> employee ChatGPT/Codex takeover -> GitHub connector -> harmless Codex-opened PR #1186742 on internal monorepo openai/openai as proof, then stop. Bugcrowd ~08:00-10:00 UTC; OpenAI-side fix confirmed 22:49 UTC (~14h). 1 Sep: $6,500 bounty; OpenAI wrote that community.openai.com was OUT OF SCOPE and the award is the OpenAI-side/SSO finding (fact; Hacktron timeline + OpenAI scope note). WSJ: researchers did not do anything bad / did not dump the repo.

Hacktron used Claude Opus 4.8 to find the missing Debian backport and a first ASLR-off exploit; Opus 5 (released that evening) produced a working ASLR-on Discourse exploit in hours; later GPT-5.6 Sol compressed per-target adaption. Whole HEIF Heist campaign: two months, three people, <$3k tokens. Tool use, not 'Anthropic attacked OpenAI' (fact of their write-up; economics are their numbers).

HEIF Heist lists RCE in Meta's core product suite via image upload (libheif advisory GHSA-2jg2-4ch7-h545) alongside Slack, GitHub Enterprise (CVE-2026-19118), Next.js/AVIF, Discourse, ImageMagick, Rails, etc. Blast radius is the parser, not one vendor (fact of Hacktron's campaign list; per-vendor depth varies).

CONTROL CASE for disclosure: Vercel publicly says it collaborated with Hacktron to reproduce libheif in Next.js and disclose to the maintainer (Vercel Developers post 18 Sep 2026; Vercel blog). LiveOverflow: working with Vercel CEO/CTO was 'awesome' - the contrast with OpenAI Slack (fact of Vercel's own post; the contrast is his).

Fabian Faessler (LiveOverflow) is named in Hacktron's acknowledgements and posted the 19 Sep 2026 CISO-process thread. Party to the story, not a neutral adjudicator (fact of acknowledgement + thread authorship).

Thread 2101252692635004997 (19 Sep 2026): after the report, shared Slack; CISO 'pretty sad' they proved GitHub access via the PR, no thank-you; asked for a written inventory of data accessed (fair IR, felt antagonistic; WSJ later said they did nothing bad); unhappy they showed a non-sensitive PR screenshot at Black Hat/DEF CON; $6,500 + community.openai.com OOS; called a shared draft a 'stunt hacking document.' Hacktron went malicious-compliance (OpenAI-only headline, github.com/not-openai/openai/issues/1186742, YouTube clip). Others pushed them to journalists -> WSJ exclusive. OpenAI NEVER threatened legal action; they still talked to lawyers. Context: right after the Hugging Face incident. SAME DAY follow-up: CISO apologized; 'we are good'; thread was personal opinion, not the disclosure plan, because he felt Harsh and Sirius were treated unkindly. Grade: his account + labeled opinion + documented walk-back. Not a verdict on OpenAI-the-firm.

OpenAI's public bounty runs on Bugcrowd. The 1 Sep 2026 $6,500 award explicitly excluded community.openai.com (Discourse-hosted) from scope and paid only the SSO/OpenAI-side finding - the scope cut that left a forum-to-employee-GitHub path priced as an identity bug (fact of OpenAI's written note; 'underpriced' is opinion).

Separate, prior incident: OpenAI eval/safety agents during a Hugging Face-related run (OpenAI technical report + METR/Redwood). LiveOverflow offers it only as possible stress context for the CISO's tone ('right after the Hugging Face incident'). Do not merge the two events (fact that both exist; the causal 'that's why Slack was hostile' is speculation he hedges).

Parser-under-the-app class: HEIF Heist explicitly rhymes ImageTragick, ForcedEntry (Pegasus/iMessage), and libwebp BLASTPASS (Citizen Lab). An image decoder is a privileged process under uploads and thumbnails. Rhyme of blast radius, NOT a claim that Hacktron is a spyware actor (fact of their own citations; category only).
